{"candidates":[{"parent":"2545cbf741dfcd43bcb1c32a1e6151e4ce623a51e7fcb663a4e15d9c84653f23","genes":{"breakout_days":120,"family":"M","momentum_days":180,"slow_days":240,"vol_target":0.18},"hypothesis":"Slower breakout (120d) and longer momentum (180d) combined with a vol target of 0.18 reduce whipsaw-driven turnover and cost drag, while the faster slow_days (240 vs 300) keeps responsiveness to the trend regime; this should raise the weak first-fold net return (0.7%) without materially increasing drawdown or concentration."},{"parent":"2545cbf741dfcd43bcb1c32a1e6151e4ce623a51e7fcb663a4e15d9c84653f23","genes":{"breakout_days":40,"family":"M","momentum_days":45,"slow_days":300,"vol_target":0.1},"hypothesis":"Faster entry (breakout 40d, momentum 45d) paired with a very slow 300d trend filter and a low 0.10 vol target should cut portfolio-level drawdown and improve Calmar, directly attacking the weak-fold concern by stabilizing the 2020-01 to 2020-07 period while keeping turnover and asset concentration contained."},{"parent":"2545cbf741dfcd43bcb1c32a1e6151e4ce623a51e7fcb663a4e15d9c84653f23","genes":{"breakout_days":55,"family":"M","momentum_days":90,"slow_days":150,"vol_target":0.15},"hypothesis":"Moderately faster breakout (55d) against a faster 150d slow filter should lift the weak first-fold return by capturing short-lived momentum, while the original 90d momentum and 0.15 vol target preserve the strong delayed-entry and no-top-3 robustness of the parent."},{"parent":"2545cbf741dfcd43bcb1c32a1e6151e4ce623a51e7fcb663a4e15d9c84653f23","genes":{"breakout_days":180,"family":"M","momentum_days":30,"slow_days":180,"vol_target":0.06},"hypothesis":"Very slow breakout (180d) with a fast 30d momentum creates an asymmetric filter that trades less and lowers both trade and asset concentration; the low 0.06 vol target reduces cost drag and improves double-cost and delayed-entry CAGRs on the weak early folds."}]}

{"candidates":[{"parent":"0916850a883eeaac257d67c60cb23ea9b970cf1b3b38c4599ba9ed2eae42d246","genes":{"atr_days":60,"breakout_days":120,"family":"N","initial_stop_atr":2.5,"risk_per_entry":0.001,"trailing_stop_atr":4.0},"hypothesis":"Combining longer 60-day ATR volatility normalization with a wider breakout horizon of 120 days and a slightly wider 2.5 ATR initial stop should filter low-quality breakouts in weak folds, reducing drawdown and improving profitable-fold fraction while keeping asset concentration in check."},{"parent":"ea1da9db475ef02239e0afafa071ce43b71da8e8fee9a741f0fc93913062ba5b","genes":{"atr_days":60,"breakout_days":180,"family":"N","initial_stop_atr":3.0,"risk_per_entry":0.001,"trailing_stop_atr":6.0},"hypothesis":"A 180-day breakout window with 60-day ATR and a looser 6 ATR trailing stop should let winners run further, countering edge decay from the top three trades by increasing the number and duration of independent trades, thus improving no_top3 trades CAGR and worst-fold return."},{"parent":"0916850a883eeaac257d67c60cb23ea9b970cf1b3b38c4599ba9ed2eae42d246","genes":{"atr_days":40,"breakout_days":80,"family":"N","initial_stop_atr":3.0,"risk_per_entry":0.001,"trailing_stop_atr":4.0},"hypothesis":"A shorter 80-day breakout with 40-day ATR aims to increase trade frequency enough to dilute single-asset and top-trade concentration, trading some per-trade edge for a more robust, higher profitable-fold fraction under realistic costs."},{"parent":"ea1da9db475ef02239e0afafa071ce43b71da8e8fee9a741f0fc93913062ba5b","genes":{"atr_days":40,"breakout_days":120,"family":"N","initial_stop_atr":3.0,"risk_per_entry":0.0025,"trailing_stop_atr":5.0},"hypothesis":"Moderate risk scaling to 0.25% per entry with the existing breakout and trailing stops should lift CAGR and Calmar without materially increasing max drawdown, while cost drag and double-cost CAGR remain acceptable and fold-level robustness improves across weak folds."}]}
